content.comment_body: Hello, I've attached a project example for a Local Area Network setup. Suppose there are two [product_name] devices, each with its own program and message. Each [product_name] would operate with a dedicated [product_name] operator panel. Based on what I've read: 1. To connect [product_name]_1 to [product_name]_1, select [product_name]_1 in Project View, choose Add Server connection, check Connect to Operator Panel, enter the IP address for [product_name]_1, and use the same TSAP for [product_name]_1. The program message should display on [product_name]_1. 2. The same method applies to [product_name]_2. Is this correct? Additionally, if device addresses are updated for the new network configuration, will this procedure still apply? Thanks in advance.

Hello [user_name], A [product_name] operator panel can connect to only one [product_name] controller. You don't need to set up a server connection for the operator panel; just navigate to the system menu under [product_name] settings and either enter the correct IP address of the controller for communication, or select it if it's already listed. If you want to show information from the second [product_name] on the first operator panel, you'll need to transfer that information between the controllers before displaying it.

Hi [user_name], First, congratulations on your expert status. I'm aware that a [product_name] operator panel can only communicate with one [product_name] controller. In the example, there are two sets: a controller and an operator panel for each. The message from the first controller will appear on its operator panel, and likewise for the second set, so no transfer is needed yet (I'll work on message transfer next). Based on your advice and what I read in the "[document]" help files, configuration should be done via Tools and Ethernet connections. I've attached details that explain how to configure this. Unfortunately, I can’t test this right now as I don’t have access to the LAN or necessary devices.

I'm not sure I understand your question fully. For communication between a [product_name] controller and its operator panel, you don't need to create a special server connection. In the operator panel system menu, under [product_name] section, simply enter or select the IP address of the controller you want to communicate with. Special connections are only necessary for communication between multiple controllers, HMIs, mobile devices, etc. Please see the attached information for details.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for guidance on correctly configuring network connections between [product_name] operator panels and their corresponding [product_name] controllers. There's some confusion about whether explicit server connections are needed, or if the IP address settings within the operator panel system menu are sufficient. The discussion reveals that clear instructional documentation is lacking regarding IP assignments and connection setup for these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a clear and concise procedure for connecting each [product_name] operator panel to its designated [product_name] controller over the network, with specific instructions that avoid unnecessary configuration steps.
